scenes.headline: Someone warned them. Nobody listened.
scenes.voiceover: In two thousand and one, one of America's most admired companies collapsed in weeks. And someone inside had already warned them.

scenes.name: Enron
scenes.headline: Debt and losses hidden off the balance sheet
scenes.voiceover: Enron looked like the future. But it used complicated side companies to keep huge debts and losses away from its main balance sheet. On paper, it looked profitable.

scenes.name: Enron
scenes.headline: The CEO quit. Then an executive spoke up.
scenes.body: Sherron Watkins warned chairman Kenneth Lay the accounting could sink the company.
scenes.voiceover: Then the C E O suddenly resigned. Executive Sherron Watkins warned the chairman that the accounting could bring the whole company down.

scenes.name: Enron
scenes.headline: Bankrupt by December 2001
scenes.voiceover: By December, Enron was bankrupt. More than seventy-four billion dollars in shareholder value disappeared.

scenes.name: Enron
scenes.headline: Prison for the CFO and CEO. The auditor fell too.
scenes.voiceover: The C F O and the C E O went to prison. Even the auditor, Arthur Andersen, collapsed.

scenes.headline: A warning that isn't acted on isn't a control.
scenes.voiceover: The lesson? A warning that isn't acted on isn't really a control.
